latest_release.name: Ardia 0.2.45
latest_release.body:
## New

- **Ardia runs on Chromium 157.** The engine moves up from 156 to 157.0.8103.38, with Helium 0.21.1's privacy patches on top, and brings Chrome 157's security fixes. Your profiles, tabs, passwords, cookies, extensions and uBlock Origin filters carry over as they are.
- **Profiles load when you open them.** At launch Ardia starts only the profiles its windows show; the rest, and their extensions, start the first time you switch to them. With eight profiles, launch memory drops from about 1.5 GB to 390 MB, and the first switch to a profile that hasn't started yet takes about two seconds. Turn it off in Settings › Advanced › Performance › "Load profiles when opened". Thanks, [@Neved4](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/802).
- **Web apps show their unread count on their tab.** Pinned tabs, Top Apps and ordinary tabs pick it up from the page title, the Badging API or a dot on the favicon.
- **WebKit pages block ads and trackers.** Pages opened in WebKit, streaming sites included, now use uBlock Origin Lite's lists and follow the same switches as the rest of Ardia: blocking on or off, the lists you picked and the sites you trust. Site Controls shows how many requests it blocked.
- **Links from pinned tabs and Top Apps open in a Peek.** A link to another site opens over the app instead of in a new tab, with Gmail, Slack and Outlook redirect wrappers unwrapped, as in Arc. Settings › Tabs › "Open new-tab links in" picks New tab, Peek or Little Ardia, and inside Little Ardia new-tab links now stay in Little Ardia by default.
- **Report a Problem, one sheet for everything.** Help › Report a Problem… (⌥⇧⌘I) takes bugs, slowness and ideas, with an optional recording of Ardia's window that never shows page contents, a short engine trace for slowness, and a preview of exactly what is sent.
- **Settings › Privacy shows how you appear to us.** An anonymous name and avatar stand in for your install's random ID, with Reset My Anonymous ID to start fresh. Under "Kept on this Mac", View My Data saves the last 7 days of what Ardia logged to your Downloads folder; it leaves your Mac only while sharing is on or when you attach it to a report.
- **Live folder tabs go back to their item.** A tab opened from a live folder keeps the item's page as its home, like a tab in a pinned group, so Back to Pinned URL takes you back to it. Thanks, [@TechSupportz](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/426).
- **The page frame goes down to edge to edge.** A slider in Settings › Appearance › Page Frame and in onboarding.
- **Drop things where you are.** Files, links and text dropped on the New Tab page open in that tab, from the Downloads popover too, and a .crx dropped anywhere in a window asks to install it.
- **Bookmarks can hide.** Turning off "Show bookmarks" in Settings › General hides the bookmark button, the bar, the Bookmarks menu and its commands, and puts Copy URL where the star was. Your bookmarks stay.
- **Organize tabs and groups from the command line.** `ardia tabs` and `ardia groups` list every window, space, group and tab as JSON, and open, move, group, nest, rename, recolour, pin, mute, sleep or close them, by name or ID, without changing the tab you're on. `ardia apply` runs a batch in one go, so you or an agent can rebuild a whole workspace.
- **Agents do more with `ardia browse`, in fewer steps.** `read` reads every matching link on a page through your logins, `script` loops across pages, HTML5 drag and drop works, and a background tab it drives keeps drawing without switching your view. `ardia computer` sets up Cua Driver so agents can use your Mac's other apps in background windows, and `ardia feedback` lets an agent tell us what got in its way.

## Faster

| | 0.2.44 | 0.2.45 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory, 1 tab | 385 MB | 288 MB | 25% less |
| Memory, 10 tabs | 908 MB | 698 MB | 23% less |
| Memory, 20 tabs | 1257 MB | 918 MB | 27% less |

With 20 tabs open, Ardia uses about a quarter less memory: every part of Chrom

detail.readme:
Touch grass.

Arc’s sidebar and Dia’s polish on real Chromium.
Free and open source. Ads and trackers stay out.

Download Ardia 0.2.45 for Mac

128 MB DMG · macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple Silicon · Notarized by Apple
Like your paint wet? The nightly has every fix the day it’s made, smudges and all.
Homebrew: brew install ardia-browser/tap/ardia
ardia.dev · What’s new · All releases · Discord

## Lose the toolbar. Move the address bar into the sidebar and the page runs all the way to the top of the window. ## Two pages, one window. Drag a tab onto the page. Up to three panes, side by side or stacked. ## Refuses to leave the picture. Switch tabs mid-video and it floats along in the corner. Go back to its tab and it slips back into the page. ## Your extensions come along. The Chrome Web Store just works, its button says Add to Ardia, and Sync takes them to your other Macs. ## Ads and trackers stay out. The full uBlock Origin is built in, cookie banners included. Google’s pings are compiled out. Crash reports are opt-in and never carry your sites or searches. ## Also in there - **Work stays at work.** Each profile keeps its own logins, history, extensions and colour. Swipe the sidebar to switch. - **Little Ardia.** ⌥⌘N opens a small window with one page and no sidebar. - **Groups on contact.** Drop a tab on a tab and they’re a group, named for you. - **Moves in for you.** Bookmarks, history, passwords and logins from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc, Dia and five more. Arc’s spaces, pinned tabs and themes too. - **Paints like Arc.** Gradient themes per profile: up to three colours, some grain, some blur. - **Syncs through your iCloud.** End-to-end encrypted, in a folder in your own iCloud Drive. No server of ours in the middle. - **Command bar.** ⌘L finds tabs, history and bookmarks, does your sums, and knows doc.new and 16 friends. - **Tidies up.** ⌥⌘K sweeps the tabs you haven’t touched into Recently Cleaned. - **Clean links.** Copy a link and the tracking junk stays behind. - **Naps when you do.** Background tabs past your latest five freeze, and sleep after half an hour. - **Sits still.** Idles under half a percent of CPU with a tab open. - **Updates itself.** Quietly, then shows you what changed. ## It’s actually Chromium. Not WebKit. Not Electron. Every window is Chrome’s own, so sites, extensions and DevTools behave like they do in Chrome. | Part | Details | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Engine | Chromium 157, on Chrome’s own framework. | ✓ Yes | | De-Googled | Google’s background services stripped out. | ✓ Yes | | H.264 and AAC | The codecs Chromium leaves out. | ✓ Yes | | DevTools | Docked, with device mode. Like Chrome. | ✓ Yes | | Sync | End-to-end encrypted, through your own iCloud Drive. | ✓ Yes | | Translate | On your Mac. Nothing leaves it. | ✓ macOS 26 | | Passkeys | Touch ID yes. iCloud Keychain waits on Apple. | ~ Partly | | Netflix and DRM | Streaming sites open in WebKit, where they play. Widevine in Chromium waits on Google. | ~ Partly | | Intel Macs | Apple Silicon only. | ✗ No |

Download Ardia 0.2.45

It’s 128 MB and one drag into Applications.
Not on a Mac? Watch › Custom › Releases up top and GitHub tells you when it is.

--- # Build it yourself A macOS browser that looks and feels like [Dia](https://diabrowser.com): Chrome's own framework from our patched Chromium with our layer on top (ArdiaCore), an Expo + React Native macOS shell, and Metal shaders reconstructed from Dia's own New Tab effects. ``` apps/ browser/ Expo + react-native-macos app (UI in src/, Xcode project in macos/) packages/ ardiacore/ The engine: Chromium 157's framework with our layer (Chrome tabs hosted in our views), JS API in src/ shell/ Native menu bar + shortcuts → JS, windows, SF Symbols, native primitives shaders/ Metal: New Tab effects + grained OKLab window backdrop import/ Import from other browsers (bookmarks, history, passwords, Arc spaces) core/ Pure TS: omnibox input → URL, suggestions, Dia-style breadcrumbs (tested) ``` ## Run it Requires Xcode 26+, CocoaPods, Node 24 (pinned in `.nvmrc`), pnpm 11. ```bash pnpm install ``` The engine (Chrome's framework, built from our patched Chromium) comes prebuilt: with no local engine build, the app's build downloads the one matching your checkout's `engine/` (about 110 MB, once; Apple Silicon only) and checks it against `packages/ardiacore/prebuilt-engines.tsv`. Every release whose engine changed publishes one. If `main`'s engine is newer than the last release's, work from a release tag (`v0.2.30`, say), or run `packages/ardiacore/scripts/fetch-engine.sh --nearest` to build against the newest prebuilt anyway. Passkeys and saved cards need our team ID and won't work in a build signed by anyone else. To change the engine itself (anything under `engine/`), build it from source: Chrome's framework from our patched Chromium tree in `~/chromium-build` (Chromium 157.0.8103.38 with the patch series in `engine/patches`; `docs/engine-build.md` › "Rebuilding", then `engine/chromium/apply.sh`, `engine/ardiacore/apply.sh` and `autoninja -C out/Release_GN_arm64 chrome_framework`; the first build takes about 2 hours). The app's build stages it from there when it exists. ```bash pnpm pods ``` In one terminal, start Metro: ```bash pnpm dev ``` In another, build and launch the Debug app (on its own data, `~/Library/Application Support/Ardia Dev`, or `ARDIA_DATA_DIR`): ```bash pnpm macos ``` Other tasks: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm shaders:check` (compiles the embedded Metal offline), `scripts/agent/build-app --config Release` (a Release `.app` with a Hermes bytecode bundle in `apps/browser/build-`, under the shared build locks; `--help`). Signed releases (DMG, Sparkle zip and appcast) are built by the Release workflow with `scripts/release.sh`, see `docs/releasing.md`. Shortcuts: ⌘T new tab, ⌘L command bar, ⌘W close, ⇧⌘T reopen, ⌘S sidebar, ⌘[ / ⌘] back/forward, ⌘R reload, ⌘1–⌘9 select tab, ⌃Tab cycle. ## How Dia's New Tab light works Dia 1.50 turns this light off along with its rebrand (a painted mark, a single-colour power-up band and a halo around the bar; `docs/dia-spec.md` › "1.50 Sunglow"), and so does Ardia. The reconstruction left the tree with it: `git show f2c0e251:packages/shaders/ios/AreaLightView.swift`. These findings come from disassembling the Metal libraries in `Dia.app` (v1.49.1) with `xcrun metal-objdump`. `BoostBrowser_PowerUp.bundle/default.metallib` contains `breathingAreaLightFragment`, which the Swift class `NewTabPage.NewTabAreaLightView` hosts. The reconstruction was `AreaLightView.swift` (above). - **The command bar is a light source.** Dia models the bar as a rounded-rectangle area light floating `lift` points above the page. Each pixel receives the closed-form irradiance of that rectangle: the solid-angle formula, one `atan` term per corner, times 1/2π. Rounded corners subtract (1 − π/4) of each corner square. The result is a physically correct penumbra: a higher lift gives a softer, wider glow. - **Falloff** is reshaped from inverse-square to `(h/d)^falloff`, where `d` is the distance to the emitter's rounded-rect surface rather than to its centre. - **Colour** is Dia's brand spectrum (`ProgressBarColor2…7` in its asset catalog): blue `#0358F7`, steel `#5092C7`, lavender `#E1E1FE`, yellow `#FFD400`, orange `#FA3D1D` and magenta `#FD02F5`. It is laid out as a wrapping, slightly diagonal gradient that scrolls every 20 s. IQ's 2D simplex noise warps the gradient under the bar, and the warp fades out into the penumbra. - **Dark mode** treats the light as HDR emission and applies the Hable/Uncharted-2 filmic tonemap (white point 11.2), with alpha set to Rec.709 luminance. **Light mode** keeps the flat palette colour and uses the irradiance as opacity. - **Finishing:** alpha fades over the top 50 pt and bottom 200 pt of the view, and ±3/255 triangular dither (Dave Hoskins' `hash12`) prevents banding in the long soft falloff. - **Animation:** the shader itself only scrolls the colours. The lift-off intro and the slow "breathing" come from the CPU, which animates `lift` and `intensity`. Those curves live in Dia's Swift code, so the ones here (quartic ease-out over 1.1 s, ±7% intensity on a 5.5 s sine) are my approximation. The **window backdrop** comes from `ARC_WindowThemeUI.bundle` (`gradientFragment` + `renderFragment`). Gradient stops are stored and mixed in **OKLab**, then converted to linear sRGB and gamma-encoded in the shader. A tiled grain texture is then multiply-blended on top. `WindowBackdropView` does the same with procedural grain. Only math and colour values are reused. No Dia images, fonts or binaries are copied into this repo. ## Architecture notes - **Why Expo SDK 54:** `react-native-macos` tops out at 0.81, which pairs with Expo SDK 54 (whose `ExpoAppDelegate` / `ExpoReactNativeFactory` have macOS code paths). - **Legacy architecture.** react-native-macos 0.81's Fabric support is experimental, so the app runs on the legacy architecture. One consequence: Expo's legacy view-manager adapter instantiates a module's *first* view class for every view it declares, so each native view has its own module. - **Metro, not `expo start`.** Metro runs through the react-native-macos CLI. `metro.config.js` redirects `react-native` → `react-native-macos` for `platform=macos`, because defining our own `resolveRequest` replaces the redirect the CLI would install. - **No Reanimated.** It has no macOS build for 0.81; animations use RN's `Animated`. - **Monorepo paths.** pnpm is set to `nodeLinker: hoisted` because CocoaPods and Metro resolve `react-native-macos` by path. The Podfile rewrites `REACT_NATIVE_PATH` to the hoisted location and raises every pod's deployment target to 14.0, since Xcode 26+ rejects the 11.0 some Expo pods declare. - **Native subviews** are sized in `setFrameSize`, not `layout()`. RN macOS assigns frames directly and never autoresizes subviews. - **Shaders** are Metal source embedded in Swift and compiled at runtime (once per class, cached). This keeps the pods free of a metallib build phase. ## Status Feature parity with Dia (everything but its AI) is tracked row by row in [docs/dia-feature-parity.md](docs/dia-feature-parity.md); releases and their notes are at [ardia.dev/release-notes](https://ardia.dev/release-notes). ## License Ardia as distributed is licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3](LICENSE), because its engine is built with GPL-3.0 patches. Ardia's own source files are under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.Apache-2.0). It builds on Chromium, carries a few of the Chromium Embedded Framework's patches to Chromium (BSD-3-Clause), and bundles uBlock Origin, each under its own license; see [NOTICE](NOTICE). Every release links its source.
